title: Bound query ranking work before relaxing latency budgets
summary: Memoize expensive ranking metadata per query and test operation counts alongside unchanged latency budgets.
reusable_steps: Memoize expensive ranking metadata per query and test operation counts alongside unchanged latency budgets
expected_outcome: When a lexical query breaks score ties with metadata, avoid repeated settings reads and metadata evaluation inside the sort comparator. Use a query-local cache keyed by hint identity, load scoped weights lazily once, and use one query-local time snapshot. Treat zero as a cached value. Do not reuse scores or weights between requests: same-scope settings can change. Preserve stable equal-score ordering, lexical priority, duplicate-source hint identity, chunk aggregation, score annotations, and input immutability. Keep no-match, singleton, and distinct-score paths lazy. Add deterministic call-count regressions and scope-refresh tests while retaining the existing wall-clock budget. A successful retry establishes intermittency, not the absence of wasted work. Keep sandbox IPC failures, resource termination, and accidentally forced provider test settings separate from product regressions; validate dependent groups in the normal CI environment and require exact-commit hosted CI.
